title: Constructible cohomological interval descent on a finite open cover
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $X=\bigcup_{t\in J}U_t$ a finite open covering [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with inclusions $u_t:U_t\hookrightarrow X$. The empty family $J=\varnothing$ is allowed when $X=\varnothing$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and derived open restriction $Lu_t^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $F\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be arbitrary, with no prior boundedness or etale-origin assumption. Then for any integers $r\leq s$: if $Lu_t^*F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(U_t,A)$ for every $t\in J$, then $F\in D_c^{[r,s]}(X,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. No Tor hypothesis is imposed. In particular, if each restriction $Lu_t^*F$ is bounded constructible with its own finite cohomological interval, then $F$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

For $X=\varnothing$ one has $F=0$, so the implication holds for every displayed interval.

proof.text: Obtain IsLocallyNoetherian X and CompactSpace X from the finite-type structure map to Spec k, and hence IsNoetherian X. The finite coefficient quotient has its published Finite instance.

Restrict intrinsic modules to constant scalars using the canonical equivalence. Pullback compatibility identifies each actual constant-ring pullback with fixed-module upperStar. The constructibility equivalence identifies the two finite global stratification predicates; it also handles the positive-stratum convention on empty schemes.

For a fixed module sheaf whose open restrictions are constructible, choose constructible etale models locally. Apply open-cover descent of the comparison counit to the degree-zero complex of this sheaf; its derived comparison direct image is bounded below by the standard right-derived lower-bound theorem. Taking H^0 produces one global etale model. Full faithfulness and comparison/pullback compatibility identify its local restrictions with the chosen local constructible models. Apply etale open locality, then comparison preserves constructibility. Thus intrinsic constructibility descends without assuming etale origin of the initial complex.

Use the same scalar equivalence and covering-family zero detection to detect zero intrinsic module sheaves. This applies to arbitrary sheaves and to the empty family on an empty scheme, and makes no geometric-stalk conservativity assumption.
The exact ordinary constant-ring pullback commutes with homology via mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. Apply the preceding constructibility and zero detection to each H^i(F).

For the fixed interval, a nonzero global H^i must remain nonzero on some member of the cover, so i lies in [r,s]. Its support is therefore finite, being a subset of the finite integer interval; every H^i is constructible by the preceding descent. This is exactly constructibleInterval.

For differing local bounds, the global support is contained in the finite union over J of the finite local supports. This union is finite even when J is empty. Descend constructibility degreewise as before. If X is empty, use the empty Fin 0 cover to make every H^i(F) zero, and use derived homology conservativity to conclude IsZero F.
